title: Callback sideband atomic idle delivery without long-thread resume
objective: Fix the measured B683 callback stall: sideband thread/resume on the very large owner thread repeatedly reaches the mux's 45-second response timeout, so the durable event survives but never delivers. For sideband callbacks only, use an atomic idle-only turn/start acknowledgement against the already extension-owned thread, park active/busy rejections durably, and remove the expensive thread/resume dependency without weakening exact-thread, dedup or fail-closed guarantees.
acceptance: Reproduce the production evidence exactly: B683 batch de917c12b5b849308db7ae562fa59a17 reached attempts>=8, hard_failure_count=1, last_failure_kind=busy/not_ready while every sideband thread/resume waited for the 45-second mux deadline; the event remained durable but undelivered.

Sideband callback delivery sends no thread/resume and no turn/steer. It issues one turn/start directly to the uniquely resolved live mux owner for the exact origin_thread_id, using the existing deterministic clientUserMessageId and callback prompt.

A successful synchronous TurnStartResponse with a valid turn id is the only delivery acknowledgement. Active/busy/activeTurnNotSteerable/already-in-progress rejections durably park without consuming the hard-failure budget; malformed, denied, wrong-owner and protocol failures retain the bounded hard-failure path.

The App Server remains the atomic concurrency authority: no local stale idle guess, no second hidden turn, no fallback App Server, no direct database injection, no VS Code reload requirement. Missing or ambiguous mux ownership stays fail-closed parked.

The subprocess transport and its resume/start-or-steer behavior remain unchanged. Existing callback, compact callback and mux suites plus focused idle-success, active-park, exact-once/restart and zero-thread-resume regression tests pass.
Document service-reload and live-canary procedure. Do not rewrite historical dead letters or mark B683 delivered synthetically.
commit_contract: NO_COMMIT. Bounded callback delivery-path repair only; Codex owns canonical acceptance, bridge service reload and B683 live canary.
